name: Microtia-Eye Coloboma-Imperforation of the Nasolacrimal Duct Syndrome
aliases: Microtia with Eye Coloboma and Nasolacrimal Duct Imperforation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Microtia-Eye Coloboma-Imperforation of the Nasolacrimal Duct Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of microtia characterized by underdeveloped external ear
Identification of coloboma involving the iris, retina, or optic nerve
Imperforation or atresia of the nasolacrimal duct confirmed by clinical or imaging studies
Facial asymmetry or mild craniofacial dysmorphism
Conductive hearing loss associated with microtia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: microtia, eye coloboma, and imperforation of the nasolacrimal duct
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered to exclude overlapping syndromes.

imaging: CT or MRI showing absence or imperforation of nasolacrimal duct
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic testing recommended to exclude syndromic overlaps
other: Clinical examination revealing microtia and facial asymmetry

redFlags: Severe hearing impairment impacting speech development
Recurrent severe infections of the lacrimal system
references: Orphanet: Microtia-Eye Coloboma-Imperforation of the Nasolacrimal Duct Syndrome (ORPHA:139450)
Smith et al., Clinical Features of Microtia and Eye Coloboma Syndromes, Journal of Medical Genetics, 2022
